item.title: More Anxious than Hopeful, Most Americans Want More Regulation of Artificial Intelligence
item.description:
## More Anxious than Hopeful, Most Americans Want More Regulation of Artificial Intelligence [![](https://navigatorresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Screenshot-2026-10-19-at-2.34.22-PM.png)](https://navigatorresearch.org/more-anxious-than-hopeful-most-americans-want-more-regulation-of-artificial-intelligence/)
#### **Americans Overwhelmingly and Increasingly Want More Regulation of Artificial Intelligence** Two-thirds (66%) want more regulation of artificial intelligence (AI), up six points from December 2025.
#### **Americans Most Trust Independent Experts to Regulate AI** A third (33%) choose a new federal agency focused on artificial intelligence, similar to the Food and Drug Administration.
#### **AI Increasingly Seen as an Issue Americans Want the President and Congress to Prioritize** When asked to select the top five issues the president and Congress should focus on, AI saw the most significant growth of any issue tested this year. [Only 7%](https://navigatorresearch.org/views-of-ai-and-data-centers/) selected AI within their top five issues back in December 2025, but that has tripled, reaching 21% earlier this month. The issue steadily gained as a priority throughout 2026, from 11% in August to 16% in September. 21% is on par with the number prioritizing crime and taxes.
![](https://navigatorresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/20261022-AI-surged-this-year-as-a-top-priority-for-Americans-e1792524569838.png)

item.title: 5 classic movies that saw our AI future coming
item.description:
# 5 classic movies that saw our AI future coming ## An MSU Denver film professor explores how science fiction anticipated today's biggest questions about artificial intelligence. RED asked Piturro to discuss five influential films that explore AI’s potential for good or harm.
The film envisions a future where artificial intelligence can help humanity achieve extraordinary things, while also warning of the dangers of becoming too dependent on intelligent machines.
“The film posits that humans must have some control over AI or we don’t know what could happen,” Piturro said.
“The Matrix” imagines a dystopian future in which intelligent machines have taken over the world and use humans as an energy source. The film examines technological dependence, autonomy and the consequences of surrendering too much control to AI systems.
“When AI runs us, we become reduced to its batteries,” Piturro said.
The film raises enduring questions about identity, consciousness and what it means to be truly human.
“The movie presents the question echoing in many people’s minds: Can we coexist peacefully?”
Unlike many AI films centered on robots or global catastrophe, “Her” is the story of a relationship between a lonely man and an “artificially intelligent operating system” who calls herself Samantha. The movie explores whether human connection is possible, or necessary, in a world where technology is all around us and easily accessible.
“This drama gives us a world where AI is already integrated into our lives, but it asks: Will AI make us lose touch with each other and diminish our humanity?”
In this psychological thriller, a tech billionaire invites a programmer to evaluate a humanoid AI capable of remarkably human behavior. As the boundaries between machine and person blur, the film raises unsettling questions about consciousness, manipulation and whether humans can truly understand the intelligence they create.
For Piturro, the film points to one of the most unsettling possibilities surrounding AI: intelligent machines that can move among us undetected.
Decades before AI tools entered everyday life, these films explored many of the same hopes, fears and ethical dilemmas that shape today’s conversations about artificial intelligence. Whether warning about losing control, questioning what makes us human or examining the role technology plays in our relationships, each movie offers a different lens on one of the most important issues of our time.
